note:
CURRENT IDENTITY CORRECTION,2026-10-29: the held filename chicago_first_swing_bridge_1849_earle.jpg and former inventory reviewer's1849 swing-bridge exclusion are wrong about this image. Exact original n24 reproduces the same lunette, including two gallows frames, high shore braces, rising closed-draw bridge profile, river vessels and foreground dockworkers/barrels. Original facing p.18 explicitly identifies the1834 bridge and says it was removed1839. Its steam vessel is not evidence that this is the1849 swing bridge. Retain the historical filename for byte/link continuity, but correct its current title/scene/description.

RETROSPECTIVE: the book credits the Chicago National Bank mural series, begun in1900 according to p.6, not a surviving1834 photograph. The source itself says the artist researched old accounts and sometimes relied on published descriptions. It does not establish an exactJuly1835 day, surveyed camera, new geographic placement, metric rise, timber scantlings, precise original finish or independence from the earlier retrospective bridge pictures. P.18 says200ft total length with60ft draw; this conflicts with other retrospective300ft texts and the independently traced current water gap. Preserve that conflict without moving the independently mapped banks or treating the mural as a measured plan. The existing sixteen-foot width is independently inferred from Norton/Moses, not measured from this image.

The source plate has been directly read. No actual native Earle camera capture or accepted matches verdict has yet been produced by this source-only packet. Baker-Co Old Point engraving keeps its separate check_required hold; none of this verifies that work's original publication.

SUBSEQUENT DIAGNOSTIC COMPARISON: the accepted sixteen-foot V5 bridge was actually rendered against this identified Earle image on 2026-10-29, including a corrected finite four-point framing. Both gallows, high outer braces, closed peaked deck, chains, boarded parapets and piled caps were compared. The camera is a reconstructed diagnostic fit; it establishes no historical viewpoint, metric dimensions or exact July-1835 condition. Fresh canonical metadata-bound capture remains a separate adoption step.
